title: Phonon Fluctuations Enhanced Superconductivity in a Three-Band Cuprate Model
abstract: The microscopic origin of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in cuprates remains an outstanding puzzle due to the interplay of intertwined orders. Experimental observations and theoretical studies have suggested crucial roles of phonons, with the $B_{1g}$ oxygen buckling mode emerging as a promising candidate. Here, we investigate the microscopic influence of this phonon in a three-band cuprate model. We find that the $B_{1g}$ phonon plays opposite roles in superconductivity depending on whether it lies in the adiabatic or antiadiabatic regime at a given temperature. Thermally populated adiabatic phonons suppress $d$-wave pairing through the loss of quasiparticle coherence, whereas antiadiabatic phonons simultaneously enhance coherence and the attractive $d$-wave pairing vertex, strengthening superconductivity across multiple diagnostics. This enhancement also exhibits pronounced electron-hole asymmetry arising from the different orbital characters of doped carriers. Our results therefore establish a microscopic mechanism through which $B_{1g}$ phonons can cooperate with electronic correlations to substantially enhance $d$-wave superconducting pairing in cuprates.
summary: This work investigates how B1g phonon fluctuations mediate high-Tc superconductivity in cuprates using a three-band model. It reveals a critical dependence on the phonon regime: adiabatic phonons suppress pairing, whereas antiadiabatic phonons cooperatively enhance d-wave pairing. The findings establish a microscopic mechanism for phonon-mediated pairing enhancement, particularly emphasizing electron-hole asymmetry.
main_problem: The paper addresses the outstanding puzzle of the microscopic origin of high-Tc superconductivity in cuprates, focusing specifically on the role of lattice vibrations (phonons).
main_result: The B1g phonon exhibits opposite roles depending on the phonon regime: it suppresses pairing in the adiabatic regime but substantially enhances d-wave pairing in the antiadiabatic regime.
method: The study employs theoretical simulations, including Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) and Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations, to analyze pairing correlations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a three-band cuprate Emery model, incorporating an electron-phonon coupling term involving the B1g oxygen buckling mode. The analysis compares the behavior in the adiabatic ($\Omega \ll 2\pi T$) versus antiadiabatic ($\Omega \gg 2\pi T$) phonon regimes.
key_observables: Dynamical Cu–Cu d-wave pairing correlator ($P_d(	au)$), largest eigenvalue characterizing pairing response ($\lambda_{\max}[C]$), and the pairing vertex ratio ($R_{3b/d}$).
important_parameters: Doping ($p=1/8$), phonon frequency ($\Omega$), and temperature ($T$). The analysis hinges on the crossover between adiabatic and antiadiabatic phonon coupling.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the B1g phonon mode is the crucial mediator, and the analysis relies on distinguishing between the temperature-dependent regimes of phonon coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of pairing correlations in both adiabatic and antiadiabatic regimes, comparing results to purely electronic models. They also show the doping dependence and the enhancement of static d-wave pairing correlations.
paper_structure: The paper develops its argument by first establishing the theoretical framework using the three-band model and phonon coupling. It then contrasts the effects of the adiabatic and antiadiabatic phonon regimes on pairing, concluding with detailed analyses of doping asymmetry and the resulting enhancement of superconducting correlations.
why_interesting: The explicit comparison between phonon regimes (adiabatic vs. antiadiabatic) provides a detailed, physically motivated mechanism for pairing enhancement, which is highly relevant to understanding how lattice dynamics influence quantum many-body states in strongly correlated systems.
